deckTitle: Plato's Dungeon Raids: The Odyssey Edition

cards.power: Hammer of Transvaluation. Breaks stable fields to force new values.
cards.gradeReason: Hammer of Transvaluation is an immediate role. Poetic-Explosive lands on first read.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Woodblock engraving. Subject: Wild-mustached philosopher smashing stone tablets with a sledgehammer. Mood: Explosive ecstatic fury.

cards.power: Civic Action / Power is created between people. / Can redirect conflict energy.
cards.gradeReason: Redirecting conflict energy is instantly playable. Battle-strategist archetype clicks at once.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Film noir sketch. Subject: Sharp-eyed woman moving pawns on a tactical map table. Mood: Precise strategic calm.

cards.power: The Gadfly Stance. Traps enemies in dialogue loops. Enemies cannot attack until they define 'Virtue'.
cards.gradeReason: Enemies cannot attack until they define Virtue is peak G1. Instant roleplay fuel, zero setup needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ancient Greek red-figure pottery. Subject: Squat bald philosopher pestering armored warrior with a wine cup. Mood: Infuriatingly cheerful.

cards.power: Radical Simplicity. Ignores all social status effects. Can sleep in Boss Rooms.
cards.gradeReason: Can sleep in Boss Rooms is maximum G1. No instruction needed. Players will just do it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Satirical engraving. Subject: Grizzled cynic in barrel ignoring a glowing boss arena warning sign. Mood: Magnificently unbothered.

cards.power: Effect: Gives quest 'Leave the Cave'. Wants you to find Truth so he can rule.
cards.lore: Quest giver or manipulator? He wrote the simulation!
cards.gradeReason: Quest-giver ambiguity is delicious but needs Zone 1 context to fully land at the table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Renaissance marble engraving. Subject: Ancient sage holding skeleton keys with shadowed cave entrance behind him. Mood: Benevolent menace.

cards.power: Why struggle? Comfort is enough. Lesson: Progress generates resistance.
cards.lore: The ultimate Netflix and Chill! Nihilistic Cozy Mode unlocked!
cards.gradeReason: Why struggle? Comfort is enough is immediately embodyable nihilistic cozy energy. Nietzsche reference fires instantly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Cozy horror illustration. Subject: Formless figure wrapped in blankets with TV remote fused to hand. Mood: Blissful existential horror.

cards.power: Effect: Players must roll Willpower or lose a turn scrolling doom-feeds. Mechanic: 'Snack Distraction'. If a player eats a real-life snack, their character sleeps.
cards.gradeReason: Real-world snack mechanic bleeds the table into reality. Performative genius that triggers itself.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Editorial cartoon. Subject: Hammock-lounging ancient Greek figure buried in chip bags and glowing phones. Mood: Cozy doom spiral.

cards.power: Ability: Quantification. Replaces descriptions with bar charts.
cards.gradeReason: Weakness: Unmeasurable things (Love, dignity, poetry) is devastating satire compressed into six words.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Corporate bureaucratic sketch. Subject: Suited figure with monitor for a head presenting a wall of bar charts. Mood: Soullessly efficient.

cards.power: Chant: 'Studies Show... Statistically Significant...' Effect: Anecdotal Evidence Rejected. Players cannot use personal experience.
cards.gradeReason: Players cannot use personal experience is the perfect boss mechanic. Every player knows this enemy.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Religious icon satire. Subject: Bearded sage surrounded by floating pie charts with a holy data-glow halo. Mood: Fanatically empirical.

cards.power: Effect: Binary Choice. Forces players to choose A or B. Both are bad.
cards.gradeReason: Good mechanic but describes a rule more than inviting a role. The Counter is the clever bit.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ancient philosopher bust. Subject: Pointing marble philosopher with two burning doorways behind him. Mood: Righteously impossible certainty.

cards.lore: It does nothing. That is its power. It anchors you to reality. Use to defeat Ideals.
cards.gradeReason: It does nothing. That is its power. Best anti-idealism relic text in the entire corpus.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Minimalist still life engraving. Subject: Single glowing pebble on stone floor surrounded by vast empty space. Mood: Profound absurd simplicity.

cards.power: Effect: Players must swap their MOOD and SKILL chips here. Danger: If you enjoy the mask too much, you can't take it off. (IT BECOMES YOUR FACE!)
cards.gradeReason: IT BECOMES YOUR FACE is pure G1 energy. Chip-swap mechanic still needs zone context though.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Theater carnival poster. Subject: Ornate Venetian mask fusing onto a warrior's face reflected in carnival mirror. Mood: Seductively horrifying.

cards.power: Effect: Idealization. Reduces complex reality to abstract concepts. Real humans burn up here.
cards.gradeReason: Real humans burn up here is haunting but the card describes the zone rather than inviting play.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Steampunk mechanical diagram. Subject: Clockwork gears and prisms reducing human figures to clean geometric shapes. Mood: Cold beautiful annihilation.

cards.power: Mechanic: Cannot be fought. Can only be survived by holding the Pebble of Imperfection.
cards.gradeReason: Cannot be fought, only survived by holding the Pebble of Imperfection. Philosophy-as-mechanic perfected.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Blinding divine light illustration. Subject: Massive blazing sun-entity looming over a tiny figure clutching a small pebble. Mood: Overwhelmingly transcendent.

cards.power: Effect: Players gain bonuses for discussing feelings but cannot [act].
cards.lore: Stay here. We can work on the character sheet forever.
cards.gradeReason: Stay here. We can work on the character sheet forever is self-aware RPG meta at its most lethal.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Cozy horror sketch. Subject: Skeleton in deck chair holding a half-finished character sheet, hammock swaying nearby. Mood: Productive paralysis.

cards.power: Mechanic: The 3d20 Borromean Throw. Rolls for Cognition, Irony, and Uncertainty. Attack: Brain Bullet Time. The game slows down. You fight your own playstyle.
cards.gradeReason: You fight your own playstyle is the perfect final boss reveal. Meta-horror and totally embodied.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Epic mythic portrait. Subject: Robed grey wizard holding three d20 dice with glowing runes, knowing smirk. Mood: Ironic omniscience.

cards.power: Cancels Ideology. Forces concrete description of reality (e.g., 'The stone is cold').
cards.lore: Reality Check! NOT a philosopher's stone!
cards.gradeReason: Cancels Ideology with a rock. The most conceptually devastating weapon in the deck.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Minimal still life engraving. Subject: Single grey pebble on white ground with NOT A PHILOSOPHER'S STONE scrawled beneath. Mood: Gloriously mundane.

cards.lore: Heavy emotional baggage inside. Send it already!
cards.gradeReason: Evocative but vague. Needs more mechanical teeth or lore specificity to reach G1.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Victorian letter illustration. Subject: Sealed wax letter with emotional weight radiating from it, monster peeking from envelope flap. Mood: Unresolved and poignant.

cards.lore: No North, only vibes. Lost but making good time!
cards.gradeReason: No North, only vibes. Lost but making good time! The Kayfabizarro ethos in eight words.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Vintage nautical illustration. Subject: Spinning compass needle going in all directions, grinning sailor on deck behind it. Mood: Joyfully directionless.

cards.power: Shows the player, not the character.
cards.lore: Break the fourth wall. Home sweet home?
cards.gradeReason: Shows the player, not the character. The perfect homecoming punchline. Fourth wall collapses instantly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ornate mirror illustration. Subject: Elaborate gilded mirror showing a modern person staring back at a Greek hero. Mood: Uncanny self-recognition.

verdict: The Philosopher's Dungeon Raid is the most structurally unusual deck in the corpus — not a card set but a full dungeon scenario document, a horizontal mythic map stitching the Odyssey to Western philosophy via dungeon crawl logic. The strength is the card design: Sokrates as Debuff-Tank, Diogenes sleeping in Boss Rooms, The Pebble cancelling ideology — these are design breakthroughs. The weakness is discoverability: without a How-to-Play overview card, first contact is disorienting. Zone numbering in the PDF is out of sequence vs the numbered zones on the map. Table-ready: YES, but needs a facilitator briefing.
blurb: A dungeon crawl through Western philosophy using the Odyssey as the map — play Sokrates, Diogenes, or Nietzsche through zones of Data Priests, Comfort Traps, and the terrifying boss The Good. For philosophy nerds, RPG tables, and anyone ever defeated by an Excel spreadsheet.

coverQA.coverVisual: 5 — Weathered parchment with octopus holding HERE BE PARADOXES sign, D20-wielding warrior, sea monsters — maximum chaos navigator energy.
coverQA.coverTitle: 5 — Red-strikethrough on THE NAVIGATIONAL CHART OF IMPOSSIBLE QUESTS revealing the actual title is conceptual perfection.
coverQA.coverVibeMatch: 5 — Every element — parchment, dice, Greek warriors, SPOILERS AHEAD, DO NOT FOLD OR CONSUME — nails the philosophical dungeon comedy tone.

coverQA.coverViral: 5 — CHECK FOR TRAPS, WHERE IS THE LOOT?!, HERE BE PARADOXES, Property of FrizzleBob the Grey — multiple shareable moments on a single page.
coverQA.coverNote: Best cover in the corpus and possibly the universe. The strikethrough title is a genre-defining meta-joke that rewards a second glance. FrizzleBob the Grey branding seal is the cherry on top. Frame it.

notes: STRUCTURAL NOTE: This is NOT a standard card deck. It is a dungeon scenario supplement / horizontal mythic map expansion with embedded card-format elements across 15 pages. Only pages 3 and 14 use the standard 2x2 card grid layout (philosopher cards and relic/artifact cards respectively). Pages 4-13 are full zone spreads (Zone 1 Troja through Zone 9 Calypso plus Final Zone Ithaka) each containing 1-2 embedded boss/hazard/trap/NPC card insets. Page 2 is the full Odyssey journey map spread. Page 15 is the Victory Condition outro page. ZONE SEQUENCE ANOMALY: PDF layout presents zones out of numerical order (Zone 6 Sirens appears on PDF page 7, Zone 5 Underworld on page 9, Zone 4 Circe on page 10) — this appears intentional, matching the non-linear Odyssey routing shown on the map. RAF boxes visible on the 4 philosopher character cards (page 3); boss/hazard/trap cards lack RAF boxes — consistency opportunity. IM Fell English SC font labeling on zone spread pages is a design annotation, not a font artifact. Victory Condition text (To win, every player must speak one sentence: What I would tell differently in the next timeline) is masterpiece one-sentence game design. FrizzleBob the Grey appears as a named final boss character — unique in the corpus.

urgent: Zone PDF page order vs zone numbers is confusing — add a page-order guide or renumber zones to match PDF layout sequence
No How-to-Play scenario overview card — first contact is disorienting without facilitator context
quickWins: Add RAF boxes to boss cards, hazard cards, and trap cards for system consistency
Add page numbers to zone spreads for quick facilitator navigation
niceToHave: A condensed 1-page scenario summary card for rapid table setup
Expand The Unsent Letter with a specific mechanic to reach its G1 potential
Consider adding Aristotle as counterpoint character card to the Plato/Sokrates axis

marketingText:
Kayfabizarro: PLATO'S DUNGEON RAIDS – The Odyssey Edition (Free Cut & Play Comic Card Game)

Western philosophy as a dungeon crawl, with the Odyssey for a map and The Good waiting at the bottom as the boss nobody beats clean.

You enter as Sokrates, or Diogenes, or Nietzsche. You cross zones of Data Priests and Comfort Traps, you take a wrong turn past the Sirens because the map is non-linear on purpose, and at the gate of Ithaka a final boss called FrizzleBob the Grey asks the only question that scores.

Plato's Dungeon Raids is not a board game with a philosophy skin. It is a Social Story Wrestling scenario: 20 cut-and-play cards, ten zones, one crooked voyage through the ideas that wrecked their own authors.

WHAT'S INSIDE?
- The Raid Deck: 20 High-Res "Print, Cut & Play" cards: philosopher characters, relics like THE PHILOSOPHER'S STONE, and the bosses, hazards and traps that hold each zone.
- The Odyssey Map: a full non-linear journey spread, Troy to Ithaka, routed the way the story actually moves and not the way a syllabus pretends it does.
- The Freestyle Rules: drop it onto your Kayfabizarro main deck or run it standalone. No math, just storytelling and the Quest Die.

WHY "PAY WHAT YOU WANT"?
I make these because a philosophy you have to play is a philosophy you finally remember. Broke? Enter "0" and take it. Want more zones? Every coin funds the next raid.

Choose your reality. Become an Epistemic Outlaw.
"To win, every player speaks one sentence: what I would tell differently in the next timeline."
Stay fluffy. — Uncle FrizzleBob
